name: What kind of warranty should I expect for a new roof?

mainEntity.name: What kind of warranty should I expect for a new roof?

acceptedAnswer.text: A new roof typically comes with two types of warranties: a manufacturer's warranty for the roofing materials and a contractor's warranty for the workmanship. Manufacturer warranties often cover defects in the materials for 20-50 years, depending on the product. Workmanship warranties, provided by the roofing contractor, usually cover installation errors for a shorter period, typically 2-10 years. It's crucial to understand the terms and duration of both warranties, including what they cover and any conditions that might void them. Always get warranty details in writing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Expect a manufacturer's warranty for materials (20-50 years) and a contractor's warranty for workmanship (2-10 years). Understand all terms in writing.
